evidence.statement: The artifact consistently reflects source distinctions among text classification, sentiment analysis, PII detection, summarization, key term extraction, language detection, and text analysis. The definition of actionable intelligence is a reasonable source-bounded interpretation, though the source does not define the phrase explicitly.

Most answers are uniquely supported by the source, but the fill-blank item accepts both “summarization” and “summary”; the source names the task “text summarization,” while “summary” more precisely names the output.
Distractors generally represent nearby source concepts, such as summarization, sentiment analysis, entity detection, and PII detection, without becoming defensible answers for the stated tasks.
Wrong options diagnose realistic confusions, including confusing spam classification with sentiment, topic extraction with language detection, and PII with useful ticket content.

The ordered sequence does not build cleanly from prerequisite concepts to application: the broad NLP relationship appears at item 10 after specialized tasks, while PII appears repeatedly across items 2, 8, and 11 and application items are interleaved with lower-level recall and sentence-ordering tasks.

The session uses multiple-choice, true/false, fill-blank, arrange-sentence, and select-all mechanics, but multiple-choice mechanics dominate the latter half and PII-related items recur with limited spacing.

Prompts vary across definitions, workplace scenarios, statements, fill-ins, and ordering tasks, though both arrange-sentence items use nearly identical generic stems and several prompts use repeated “Which task/approach should...” wording.

The support-ticket, review-routing, customer-comment, and wider-team sharing scenarios resemble credible workplace text-analysis decisions and align with the source's customer feedback and support-ticket use cases.

Incorrect-answer feedback usually identifies the confused concept and gives a corrective next step, especially for classification, language detection, and PII items; some recall and ordering items provide only brief generic explanations.
The session mixes remembering, understanding, and applying items, with workplace applications suitable for a Level 2 unit on identifying common text-analysis tasks.

Core terms are used consistently with the source, including text classification, sentiment analysis, PII detection, key term extraction, language detection, summarization, NLP, and unstructured text. The only minor inconsistency is accepting “summary” alongside the named technique “summarization.”

The artifact is source-faithful and varied enough to be usable, but the exact sequence feels conceptually scattered, repeats PII disproportionately, and delays the broad NLP/text-analysis framing until near the end.

largest_gap.summary: The exact item order does not scaffold from broad framing and foundational distinctions into workplace application.

evidence.statement: The source establishes text analysis as a subset of NLP and introduces common tasks before application, but the artifact places the NLP framing at item 10 and interleaves repeated PII checks with unrelated recall, ordering, and application items.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Reorder the existing item objects only: present the broad NLP/text-analysis framing first, then foundational task-identification items, then related distinctions and PII protection, and finish with integrated workplace applications. Preserve every item object, payload, question_type, and deterministic answer exactly; set no payload fields.

result.concise_summary: The session is largely source-faithful, unambiguous, and pedagogically usable, but its exact order is scattered and repeats PII disproportionately. A safe session-level reorder is the largest improvement; absent approved references modestly lowers confidence but does not require human review.
